ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and substantiated UBOs against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and the annual official Spanish BOE sanctions notices; mandatory politically exposed persons ('PEP') risk classification under Ley 10/2010 for resident and foreign public officials; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk third-country source of funds, and cash-intensive or crypto-adjacent transactions; all screening records must be maintained for at least 10 years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación social via the Colegio de Registradores de España online portal (www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Spanish or in a perfectly transliterated Latin alphabet equivalent; Spanish accent marks are permitted; the name must be unique, not contrary to law, not identical to an existing Spanish company denomino, and must not be misleading as to the actual activity of the SL. Names in other languages are accepted only where correctly transliterated into Latin script and sufficiently distinctive.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Palabra que induzca a error sobre el objeto social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name certificate is rejected on grounds of identity, misleading character, or prohibited words, the applicant may request a reasoned new filing before the Registro Mercantil Central with corrected alternatives or submit an administrative appeal within one month of the rejection notification. The formal remedy is the 'recurso de alzada' filed with the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (now Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) through the electronic records of the Ministry of Justice. If judicial review is required, the applicant may later file 'recurso contencioso-administrativo' before the Audiencia Nacional within two months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered agent address is permissible for an online retail SL engaged in ISIC 4791 e-commerce, provided it is a real Spanish address equipped to receive notifications to the Registro Mercantil, tax authorities, and social security. The tax administration will assess substance factors such as genuine management decisions being taken in Spain, local employees or adequate outsourcing, storage or warehouse arrangements, and active bank accounts. A pure virtual mailbox with no operational Spanish presence increases the risk of Portuguese or Spanish permanent establishment and place-of-management challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; the annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk e-commerce SL carrying no statutory license is estimated at under 5%. Occasional administrative inspections may nonetheless occur for VAT compliance, consumer protection, and verification that the registered office is genuine. Financial and tax audits, which may involve premises visits, remain possible.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) via Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). For the common-regime SL, AEAT is the sole competent authority for state-level corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding taxes; the Basque Country and Navarre have separate Haciendas Forales applicable only if the entity were domiciled there.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Obtain NIE for each non-resident shareholder and director through the Spanish consulate or National Police; 2) Execute the public deed of incorporation before a notary and apply for provisional NIF (formerly CIF) with the territorial AEAT office; 3) File Form 036 (Census Declaration) within one month after constitution to register for Corporate Income Tax, VAT, and employee withholdings; 4) For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in Spain, appoint a fiscal representative for VAT and Non-Resident Income Tax purposes; 5) Obtain definitive NIF, activate AEAT digital certificate (electronic ID) for electronic filing, and complete the OSS registration if selling goods remotely to Spanish consumers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. A Spanish SL is automatically a taxable entity under the Corporate Income Tax Act (Ley 27/2014). Elective regimes include: the Spanish tax consolidation group election (Articles 58-70 LIS) for groups of resident entities (80%+ ownership); the centralized VAT OSS/MOSS special scheme election for e-commerce distance sales; the option between territorial and imputation regimes for controlled foreign corporations under Article 100 LIS; and hybrid mismatch treatment as adjusted through Article 15n LIS (ATAD).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis economic threshold: any taxable person performing taxable supplies in Spain must register for VAT before commencing activities. For non-established e-commerce operators, the EU OSS intra-Community distance sales threshold is EUR 10,000; exceeding it triggers Spanish VAT on B2C supplies and requires OSS registration with AEAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) quasi-real-time VAT book reporting for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6 million, with records transmitted to AEAT by API within 4 calendar days; mandatory B2B e-invoicing under the Crea y Crece framework and Verifactu (Royal Decree 1007/2023) requiring certified billing software with interoperable QR-coded electronic invoices and validation signature; no Italian-style centralized digital stamping, but AEAT performs automated cross-checking of invoices, customs declarations, and SII/Verifactu records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 21 LIVA for supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the seller (or a third party on behalf of the seller) to a third-country (non-EU) destination, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within three months from delivery and the vendor retains full documentary evidence; ancillary international transport and freight services directly linked to export goods also qualify for 0% under the same provision.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) with valid exit and export validation by the Customs Office
Bill of Lading, CMR Waybill, or Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch to the non-EU destination
Commercial Invoice and Packing List with itemized goods, values, and HS codes
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit confirmation) documenting receipt of export proceeds
Insurance certificate and transport documents showing arrival at destination, where available
Export license or dual-use clearance certificate if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT monitors exports through the Integrated Management System of Customs Operations and SII analytics. If goods do not leave the EU within 90 days or the export documentation is false or incomplete, the 0% rate is revoked retroactively, and the exporter is charged 21% VAT with statutory late-payment interest; material infractions carry administrative penalties of 50% to 150% of the defrauded tax amount; fraudulent schemes exceeding EUR 120,000 in evaded VAT trigger criminal liability under Article 305 of the Criminal Code; the four-year statute of limitations permits retrospective reassessment and irreversible clawback of refunds, and joint and several liability attaches to persons who issued or knowingly used false export certificates.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the national competent authority within the Eurosystem and as the supervisory body of the Spanish banking sector; the European Central Bank (ECB) as the issuer of the euro and operating authority of TARGET2/T2S settlement infrastructures; SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias), jointly hosted by Banco de España and CNMV, as the national financial-intelligence unit and AML/CFT enforcement body under Law 10/2010.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the euro. There is no exchange-control statute, no central-bank prior authorization requirement for resident SLs acquiring foreign currency, and no restriction on the repatriation of share capital, dividends, liquidation proceeds, royalties, or intercompany loan repayments. The legal basis is Articles 63-66 TFEU, Directive 88/361/EEC, and the Spanish balance-of-payments liberalization regime (Law 18/1992 as amended). Residual encumbrances are purely fiscal and documentary: (i) dividend remittances to a non-resident beneficial owner trigger a 19% IRNR withholding tax where no treaty reduction applies, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) when the parent holds at least 5% of the SL's capital for at least one year, and further reduced under applicable double-tax treaties; (ii) the paying bank requires the SL to file quarterly Model 216 non-resident tax returns and attach tax-residence certificates for the beneficial owner before releasing funds abroad; and (iii) each cross-border payment must be tagged with a Banco de España statistical balance-of-payments purpose code, as transmitted by the bank, but this is a reporting formality and never a permission gate. Profit remittance to a majority EU parent can therefore be executed with zero withholding and no prior authorization, subject solely to the annual-accounts approval and dividend distribution rules of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender obligation, no statutory conversion timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Spain. Since the full liberalization of the former peseta exchange-control regime and Spain's integration into the euro area, a Spanish SL may retain export receivables in EUR, USD, CNY, or any other currency indefinitely, in domestic or foreign bank accounts, and may freely net or invest those proceeds. The only surviving obligations are statistical and customs-related: (i) the banking channel assigns balance-of-payments purpose codes to incoming export wires on the SL's behalf; (ii) goods exports require a customs DUE/SAD declaration through the AEAT (Tax Agency) showing invoice, HS code, and value consistency; (iii) intra-EU dispatches require Intrastat periodic declarations where volume thresholds are met; and (iv) services-related exports to non-EU countries must be captured in the AEAT 'Declaración de Transacciones Exteriores' reporting. None of these obligations imposes any conversion or repatriation timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary EUR Operating Account (IBAN ES-series) plus, where required by the notary, a temporary Capital Formation Deposit Account (cuenta de aportación) to obtain the certificado de desembolso del capital social; supported by DayOne fintech/e-commerce onboarding desk.

Primary EUR Operating Account with integrated SWIFT MT103 correspondent banking, FX forward desk, and delegated PSP collection arrangements; capital formation certificate can be issued pre-registration.
Primary EUR Operating Account plus digital SME platform ('BBVA Negocio') suitable for remote monitoring of inbound Stripe/PayPal settlements and automated AEAT tax payments.
Primary EUR Operating Account aligned with BStartup growth banking; offers purpose-code automation for BOP and SEPA instant acquisition for treasury sweeps.
Secondary EUR Operating Account; more selective lending appetite for low-asset e-commerce SLs, but viable for a merchant settlement reserve account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, strictly as a secondary treasury overlay. Legal constraints: a Spanish SL may lawfully hold funds with an EU-authorized e-money institution (EMI) under Law 21/2011 and the EMD2/MiCA framework, including Spanish-licensed EMIs or passported ones (e.g., Revolut Business, Qonto), with remote eIDAS video identification. However, the EMI channel is not viable for: (i) the statutory paid-in capital certificate required by the Spanish notary during incorporation (the certificado de desembolso must come from a credit entity supervised by Banco de España); (ii) primary collection of Stripe/PayPal marketplace funds where the settlement accounts attract SEPBLAC scrutiny of unlicensed e-money activity; and (iii) trade-finance instruments such as documentary credits. EMIs also sit outside the Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos (Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme), holding client funds under safeguarding provisions instead. Recommended use: multi-currency expense cards, low-value supplier disbursements in USD/CNH, and a sweeper account that daily empties to the primary banking platform; funds must never be permitted to accumulate above EUR 20,000 in the EMI to avoid elevated layering risk flags.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Spanish Tier-1 banks require at least one physical appearance for the final execution of the treasury mandate when the SL is owned by non-residents. The legal representative (administrador único or an apoderado with a sufficiently broad power of attorney) must attend a branch meeting for identity verification and signature of the account agreement. A power of attorney granted abroad must be notarized, apostilled under the Hague Convention of 1961, and, where it is granted by a legal entity, accompanied by certified corporate documents of the grantor. Fully remote video-identification onboarding is legally possible for EU-resident signatories holding a valid NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero), but banks retain absolute discretion and generally escalate any corporate account with a 'hydroponics' trade description to enhanced due diligence, which then requires an in-person interview. Because the formation of the SL itself mandates a physical appearance before a Spanish notary for the escritura de constitución, the optimal sequence is to execute the bank opening during the same trip in which the notarial deed is signed; this satisfies the KYC interview requirement as a de facto matter and accelerates treasury activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Description of corporate purpose containing 'hydroponics' and 'garden equipment' triggers an automated red flag for narcotics-precursor and cannabis-cultivation association (grow tents, LED cultivation lamps, nutrient schedules), potentially escalating the file to SEPBLAC reportable status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (a) official company-objects clause translation demonstrating ISIC 4791/NAICS 444220 classification as online retail of home gardening and hydroponic supplies; (b) a photographed and itemized product catalogue showing consumer-grade LED grow bulbs, open-shelf hydroponic kits, pH meters, and inert growing media, with an affirmative statement excluding equipment exclusively used for clandestine cultivation (e.g., sealed grow tents, carbon scrubbers with dual-use overload); (c) a published terms-of-sale excerpt prohibiting unlawful cultivation use and an age-gating policy; (d) sample customer invoices showing low-ticket B2C value; (e) a written AML policy for the SL, including refused-transaction logging and dual-use screening guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% non-resident ownership of a newly incorporated SL with subscribed capital at the statutory EUR 1 minimum raises concern that the entity lacks economic substance, is a letterbox entity, or will be used for pass-through financing or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (a) notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) with full shareholding schedule; (b) Registro Mercantil certificate of inscription; (c) UBO registration receipt from the Registro de Titularidades Reales; (d) CRS/self-certification Form 925 for every direct shareholder; (e) tax-residence certificates of shareholders; (f) a source-of-wealth statement for the injected capital; (g) a realistic substance plan showing leased or virtual office in Spain, local logistics partner, and director engagement; (h) a 12-month treasury forecast demonstrating that the EUR 1 capital is complemented by pending shareholder loans or contributions for inventory procurement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-value inbound settlement flows from Stripe and PayPal into the SL account, when combined with daily sweeps to an EMI or to a foreign parent, pattern-match to unlicensed payment-institution activity or to layering across jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (a) signed merchant agreements with Stripe and PayPal in the SL's name, with Merchant ID numbers visible; (b) PSP settlement schedules and payout description fields linking every payout batch to underlying card transactions; (c) three months of granular settlement statements; (d) a chargeback/dispute ratio report under 0.5%; (e) an account-policy letter committing that PSP proceeds settle only in the primary domestic operating account and are disbursed exclusively to pre-registered trade suppliers and AEAT tax payments; (f) quarterly reconciliation packs to be provided upon bank request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound wires to Asian component manufacturers (e.g., Shenzhen light-fixture and pump suppliers) for hydroponics-related hardware attract correspondent-bank scrutiny on jurisdiction risk, goods description mismatch, and possible dual-use export controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (a) per-shipment dossier comprising purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading/airway bill with HS codes aligned to the goods description; (b) supplier business-license translation and sanction-screening certificate; (c) a tariff classification memo confirming the goods are LED power supplies (HS 8504) and plastic irrigation fittings (HS 3917/3926), not controlled dual-use items; (d) declaration that the SL holds an EORI number and files customs entries in Spain; (e) commitment to execute first orders above EUR 50,000 through a documentary letter of credit under UCP 600 rather than open-account telegraphic transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Short corporate history and initial shareholder-loan funding occurring in the weeks before revenue commencement triggers bank suspicion of round-tripping, mismatched purpose codes, or attempted evasion of foreign-asset declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (a) shareholder loan agreement with commercial interest rate and repayment schedule; (b) bank reference letter from the remitting bank of the shareholder; (c) 12-month cash-flow budget linking the borrowed funds to specific inventory purchase orders and 3PL onboarding in Spain; (d) contracts with the Spanish fulfillment provider and logistics partner; (e) a signed management representation letter confirming no round-tripping transactions and no unreported foreign bank accounts (Form 720 is filed annually for non-Spanish assets exceeding EUR 50,000); (f) receipts of the initial corporate tax (Modelo 200) and VAT (Modelo 303) filings to demonstrate tax-bank integration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for non-resident equity injection: (1) Before incorporation, open a temporary capital formation account (cuenta de aportación) in the name of the 'Sociedad en formación' using the provisional NIF, and instruct the shareholder to wire the subscribed capital in EUR via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer if the remitter is in the EEA) precisely to that account; the remitter name must exactly match the registered shareholder name to avoid a blocked-funds incident. (2) In the remittance information field, quote the notarial deed reference and the code 'APORTACIÓN CAPITAL SOCIAL / CONSTITUCIÓN SL' plus the provisional NIF; the bank assigns its Banco de España balance-of-payments purpose code for direct-investment equity capital, which the SL must confirm at onboarding. (3) The bank issues the certificado de desembolso del capital social to the notary; post-notarization and inscription in the Registro Mercantil (Mercantile Registry), the funds are reclassified as paid-in equity and transferred to the main operating treasury account. (4) Compliance verification at the inbound stage: for wires above EUR 10,000, the bank requires a source-of-funds declaration and, where the shareholder is an entity, its certificate of good standing plus UBO disclosure; for any subsequent shareholder loan or capital increase, the same documentary chain is required. (5) No forex conversion is required because the injection is in EUR; if a shareholder injects USD, the conversion executes at the bank's spot rate and the operation is reported with the same BOP equity-purpose code, but this unnecessarily complicates the audit trail and should be avoided.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails ranking for a Spanish e-commerce SL sourcing garden hydroponics hardware: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) for all EUR payables to EEA/UK suppliers, settlement T+0/T+1 with no bank approval; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA suppliers (China, Vietnam, United States) in EUR, USD, or CNH, routed through the bank's correspondent network, with mandatory 70-field remittance details (invoice number, HS code, purchase-contract reference) and a BOP purpose code corresponding to merchandise imports; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit subject to UCP 600 and e-UCP for first transactions from high-risk jurisdictions or for orders above EUR 50,000, issued at sight or 30-day usance with confirming-bank option; (iv) Open-account trade with 30-60 day supplier terms once credit history is established, supplemented by supply-chain finance or credit insurance (CESCE or private insurers) where the SL wishes to extend supplier days; (v) import duties and VAT are paid exclusively through the customs broker's AEAT deposit schedule or via the 'Cuenta Corriente Aduanera', never through merchant wires; all B2B cash or non-bank settlement is statutorily limited in Spain (Law 7/2012, as amended) and must be avoided entirely. Every outbound wire must fall within the SL's declared KYC business purpose; payments to third parties not listed in the approved supplier registry trigger automatic suspension and EDD review, so the supplier master list must be filed with the bank at onboarding and updated quarterly.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, subject to EMIR uncleared margin requirements; available once the SL signs the bank's Elective Professional Client questionnaire.
FX swap (spot-forward combination) for rolling monthly conversion of USD settlement proceeds from PSPs into EUR operating liquidity.

Zero-cost collar (tunnel) EUR/USD, combining a purchased USD-call with a sold USD-put at predefined strikes, to protect e-commerce gross margin on forecast outbound procurement without premium outlay.
Participation forward and turbo option structures that preserve partial upside if EUR softens while capping maximum cost on USD purchases.
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) strictly for circumstances where the SL assumes USD-denominated shareholder debt or significant USD capex liabilities above EUR 500,000.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): expressly classified as not advisable and generally structurally unavailable for EUR because the euro is fully convertible and a deep deliverable market exists; NDFs carry collateral friction and pricing opacity in the EEA and must not be used for EUR/USD or EUR/CNH exposures.

Offshore CNH deliverable forwards executed via the bank's Hong Kong/Shanghai booking channel for CNY supply-chain payables, but only as a complement to natural EUR/CNY offset from any CNY customer receipts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Cuentas Anuales): balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, annual report, and audit report when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the province of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; approval must occur within 6 months of fiscal year-end (calendar-year SL: approval by June 30; deposit by July 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 1,200-12,000 imposed by the Mercantile Registry; statutory closure of the corporate file (cierre registral) barring all subsequent registrations until filed; public disclosure as a non-depositing company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legalization of statutory corporate books (Libro de Actas, Libro Registro de Socios, and accounting books)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year SL: by April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 12,000; unlegalized books lose evidentiary value and cannot be used in commercial or tax disputes; registry filing privileges may be suspended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (Declaración de Titular Real / UBO statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales (central beneficial-owner registry managed by the Colegio de Registradores)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval of annual accounts; any change in ownership must be filed within 10 days of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EUR 600-10,000 for non-filing; EUR 10,000-60,000 for false, inaccurate, or incomplete data (art. 51, Ley 10/2010).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 1-25 immediately following the fiscal year-end (within 25 calendar days after 6 months from year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5%-20% of tax due (5% per month of delay); late-payment interest; minimum penalty of EUR 200 when no tax is due; potential criminal liability for intentional concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1-30 following the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed fine of EUR 200 for late filing with no tax due; 5%-20% surcharge plus late-payment interest when VAT is due; proportional penalty up to EUR 20,000 for incorrect data.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if, for two consecutive fiscal years, the SL meets at least two of the following: (i) total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; (ii) net turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for consolidated groups, listed entities, or entities of public interest.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC) per RD 1514/2007 as updated by RD 1/2021; consolidated financial statements may apply IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Real Decreto 609/2023, the SL must file an annual beneficial-owner statement with the Registro de Titularidades Reales within one month of shareholder approval of annual accounts. Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 10 days of the relevant registration or transaction. The statement must identify all natural persons directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights; if no such person exists, the natural-person senior managers must be disclosed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas (Minute Book of shareholders and directors' meetings)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and Annual Accounts Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,900-4,800 per audit (when mandatory threshold is triggered)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for the first two years of taxable profits for newly created entities; tax credits for R&D and technological innovation; participation exemption for dividends and capital gains from qualifying subsidiaries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) - filed electronically via the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) online portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days after the end of the 6 months following the fiscal year-end (e.g., for fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is 25 July of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (Base imponible) - net income after adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report income attributable to a Spanish permanent establishment (PE) only; non-residents without a PE are not subject to corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate (Tipo de gravamen) - standard 25% or reduced 15% for new entities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the rate applicable to the entity's status; non-resident PEs use the same rates as resident entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability (Cuota íntegra) - taxable base multiplied by tax rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate based on the PE's taxable income; deductions and credits may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and credits (Deducciones y bonificaciones) - e.g., R&D tax credits, double taxation relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only those credits available to non-resident PEs under domestic law or tax treaties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable (Cuota líquida) - after deductions and withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure any withholding taxes on income paid to the PE are correctly credited.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due per month of delay, up to 100% of the tax; daily surcharges of 0.5% for late payment; additional penalties for inaccurate or incomplete data.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 202 (Pago fraccionado) - quarterly advance payment filed electronically via AEAT
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 20 days after the end of each quarter: 20 April (Q1), 20 July (Q2), 20 October (Q3), 20 January (Q4 of previous year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base for the quarter (Base del pago fraccionado) - based on the profit of the preceding fiscal year or current year estimate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must make quarterly payments on the same basis as resident entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable percentage (Tipo de gravamen) - typically 18% for large companies, 15% for others
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the rate corresponding to the entity's size and tax regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable (Importe a ingresar) - calculated as percentage of the base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the amount due; may be reduced by prior quarterly payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount due per month, up to 100%; interest on late payment; potential surcharges for underpayment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (for non-residents, unless reduced by a tax treaty or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority and submit it to the Spanish paying entity before the dividend distribution. The paying entity must retain the TRC and apply the reduced withholding rate. For EU/EEA shareholders, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive may allow a 0% withholding rate if the shareholder holds at least 5% of the capital for at least 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 19% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates may reduce to 0-10% depending on the treaty. For EU, the Interest and Royalties Directive may allow 0% if the beneficial owner is a qualifying EU company.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 10,000,000 EUR (net turnover) triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; additionally, transactions with related parties exceeding 250,000 EUR require contemporaneous documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but requires economic substance for tax residency and anti-abuse purposes. The company must have real management, employees, and business activity in Spain to avoid being classified as a shell company. The General Anti-Abuse Clause (GAAC) and Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC) rules apply to prevent artificial arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or failure to file tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax amount evaded; criminal penalties including imprisonment up to 6 years for fraud exceeding 120,000 EUR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for tax debts if they participated in or negligently allowed the evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and asset seizure possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a company without real economic activity, solely to avoid tax or launder money
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Company may be disregarded for tax purposes; penalties up to 150% of tax evaded; criminal charges for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for corporate debts, travel bans, and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with AML obligations, such as customer due diligence, record-keeping, or reporting suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 150,000 EUR for serious breaches; criminal liability for money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable and imprisoned; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.
